title: The Transformer
tagline: Self-attention, multi-head attention, positional encodings, the Transformer block and its variants
summary: Since 2017 the Transformer has been the architecture of language models. This course derives self-attention and multi-head attention, positional encodings, the residual Transformer block, the encoder, decoder and encoder–decoder variants, the cost of attention, and the efficient and sparse variants used at scale.

overview: The transformer architecture — attention, positional encoding, and feedforward layers — is the backbone of all modern LLMs. This course covers multi-head attention and the transformer block.
Scaled dot-product attention with multiple heads allows each layer to mix information from arbitrary input positions. Residual connections and layer normalization stabilize deep stacks.
outcomes: Trace the transformer block forward pass: Q, K, V, softmax, residual, norm.
Explain multi-head attention and why multiple heads help.
Compare positional encoding schemes: sinusoidal, learned, RoPE.
Describe causal masking and its role in autoregressive generation.
